title.narrative: Supporting Inclusive, Continuous and Community-led Humanitarian Response in Jamaame and Afmadow Districts in line with the Flagship Initiative.

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project by Humanitarian Africa Relief and Development Organization (HARD) will support Inclusive, Continuous and Community-led Humanitarian Response in Jamaame and Afmadow Districts as per with the Community Engagement component of the Somalia Humanitarian Fund’s Standard Allocation 2 (2025) Flagship Initiative in Afmadow and Jamaame districts, Juba land. The project will help communities formulate and rank CEPs, sustain engagement across implementation, and harvest learning to guide community-led humanitarian programming in the two districts.lt/pgtltpgtHARD is a National NGO that has served communities in Jamaame and Afmadow since its inception, providing community-led initiatives. The organization has a good relationship with the local communities and administrations, built over years of consistent mutual engagement in community service.lt/pgtltpgtThe initiative will place affected populations at the center of humanitarian response, ensuring that interventions directly reflect community-defined priorities. Both districts face severe humanitarian pressures, with Afmadow hosting nearly 50,000 people in IPC Phase 3 or above (including 37,000 IDPs) and Jamaame hosting more than 62,000 of which 33,300 are rural households facing acute food insecurity (FSNAU, Aug 2025).lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn line with the Flagship Initiative, HARD will facilitate structured consultations through Focus Group Discussions, Community Assemblies and inclusive dialogues anchored in Area-Based Coordination (ABC) structures. Women, youth, persons with disabilities and minority groups will be meaningfully represented, ensuring equity, accountability and protection. lt/pgtltpgtCommunity priorities will be ranked, costed and documented in District-specific Community Engagement Plans (CEPs), which will directly inform the Implementation Envelope of the SHF Allocation for Afmadow and Jamaame. By strengthening ABC capacity in participatory methodologies and embedding community voices into decision-making, the project will enhance trust, transparency and local ownership. lt/pgtltpgtExpected results include stronger accountability of humanitarian actors to affected populations, improved coordination between communities and responders, and the generation of robust CEPs that provide the evidence base for life-saving and inclusive interventions. HARD’s proven expertise in participatory approaches and long-standing presence in Juba land makes it well positioned to deliver this flagship engagement.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtHARD will closely engage and work with all stakeholders to ensure successful delivery. These include OCHA HFU/SHF, other CE partners and technical support provider ASEP and its partner. HARD will also collaborate with the ABC structures, OCHA FCU and other coordination Forums to ensure sharing of information, knowledge, learning and seamless coordination.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project begins with HARD participating in a three-day workshop organized ASEP as the technical support lead. The workshop will provide inception, co-design and training to build a shared foundation on CE principles and methodologies across the four CE districts of Baidoa, Jowhar, Jamame and Afmadow.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtHARD will then conduct the initial community engagement in Afamdow and Jamame to support communities develop their CEPs. Thereafter, monthly community engagement will be held over the implementation period. HARD will also participate in the quarterly learning and analysis sessions with other CE parters, HFU and ABCs, culminating in a joint End-of-Project reflection Workshop to consolidate lessons learned for future Flagship programming.lt/pgt
